summary.fallback: Bring back raider proof from the outpost road and test the village champion's story.

intro.fallback: Stranger, have you heard the tale already? Our champion has told it loudly enough for half the village to know every heroic breath he claims to have taken.

offer.fallback: A man who says he drove raiders from an outpost alone, saved two villagers, and returned with a medal taken from their captain. The children cheer when he passes.
Because heroes usually grow quieter after bloodshed, not louder. His story shines too cleanly, and no one who was supposedly saved has come forward to bless his name.
What do you want from me?

Go to the outpost road and bring back a raider's crossbow and a scrap of leather armor. If his battle was real, the field will tell us. If it was bought, stolen, or invented, the field may tell us that too.

return.fallback: A crossbow, worn leather, and not a single mark that matches his tale. Either the outpost forgot him, or he was never there as he claimed.

reward.fallback: Take these for your road dust. I need you for one more thing: someone survived that night, and I think our hero has been praying no one finds him.

done.fallback: The trophy never sat right with me. Now I know why.
